facts.value: Meredith Corporation (NYSE: MDP), containing NMG and LMG before separation. This process offers selected stations and then LMG; Gray acquires the surviving Meredith legal entity holding LMG after NMG is spun off.
Gray Television, Inc., through its subsidiary Gray Hawkeye Stations, Inc. (Merger Sub).

$16.99 per share in cash (amendment of 06/02/2021; EV $2.825B). The original price was $14.51 per share in cash (05/03/2021; EV $2.7B, of which $725M was cash to shareholders after $1.975B net debt stayed with LMG RemainCo). Shareholders also receive one NMG SpinCo share per Meredith share in the spin-off. Under the 10/06/2021 Dotdash (IAC) agreement those shares are to be sold for $42.18 cash each; that deal is not a condition of the Gray merger.
Fall 2019: preliminary talks with a few private equity firms, including Party B, about possible strategic transactions. None went beyond preliminary talks and no transaction resulted (p.58, p.60).
Met (process 1): 17 parties (confidentiality agreements with 17 parties including Gray, p.60)

Yes under the provisional legal-entity convention: proposals for LMG RemainCo are coded Bid. Economically they acquire LMG after separation of NMG, not pre-separation Meredith including both businesses. Coding remains for Alex under Q7. Meredith is excluded from structural estimation and retained for descriptive/reduced-form use.

facts.value: US dollars. Station proposals use aggregate millions; LMG proposals generally use enterprise values in billions. Party D combines cash for debt refinancing/dividends with equity in a new company; its per-share dividends exclude that equity. Gray’s $14.51/share cash was agreed May 1–2 before signing. Mixed bases: Q4.
Cooley LLP (Deloitte Tax LLP was tax adviser; regulatory advisers not named)

Meredith offered four stations through outreach starting November 16, 2020; 20 parties contacted, 17 NDAs. December advancement into diligence preceded final station offers requested January 12, 2021, while Gray/B pursued LMG. Board paused stations January 28; Gray and B received final LMG solicitations March 17, and D was admitted to the documentation stage March 30. Gray preferred April 23; May 1–2 debt allocation fixed $14.51 before May 3 signing/announcement. D’s post-signing bids led to June 2 amendment at $16.99. Alex excluded structural estimation because acquired LMG has no unaffected market price; retain for descriptive/reduced-form use.

cells.Question: One continuing process with four rounds: initial station outreach (November 16), advanced diligence (after December 21), first final station solicitation (January 12), and final LMG solicitation (March 17). Should January 28’s pivot to LMG open an additional stage?
cells.Recommended answer: Keep four rounds provisionally. January 12 independently opens a round under E6; do not retroactively call December advancement final. Keep January 28 within round 3 pending the separate stage judgment.
cells.Why, with page: December advancement and January 12 first-final request are distinct (pp.60–61). Gray/B continue LMG diligence (pp.62–63), so E5 does not establish a process break. Fall 2019–November 2020 predates the organized process; June 2–October 6 follows signing.
cells.What changes if answered differently: An additional January 28 stage would move subsequent pre-March 17 events to round 4 and final LMG events to round 5; offer facts remain unchanged.
